text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.
-One out of ten Norwegian doctors has seriously considered to commit suicide. Their numbers mainly include psychiatrist, a study shows.

-The Central Bank and the Norwegian Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission disagree on whether Den Norske Bank (DnB) must be transformed into a holding company following its acquistion of life insurer Vital Forsikring. According to the Banking, Insurance and Securites Commission, the current company structure means financial problems in Vital could affect DnB's banking business unproportionally hard.
-Environmentalists protest against Orkla-owned Borregaard's plans to bulid an energy plant. It would increase Norway's carbone dioxide emissions by one percent, the environmentalists say.

-Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland has pledged 500 million crowns for a fund which would make it easier for companies to use new environmental technology. He insists Norway should build two hotly disputed naturan gas power plants.
-International icecreame producers may enter the Norwegian market although Norwegian producers are struggling for profit.
-Almost 500,000 Norwegians have Internet at work, an increase of 20 percent since March. In total, 1.1 million Norwegians have access to Internet.
